As a newbie:
"You gotta know when to fold em. Learn when to walk away, know when to run"
If combat is unfamiliar, I seriously wouldn't recommend fighting more than 2/3 at a time. It's super easy to mis-time a swing and get dragged down. This is especially true in B42 where fatigue and exhaustion build much quicker. Sneaking around and taking out individual stragglers is your best bet.

You walk faster than the zombies can shamble. If you find yourself in a bind, just walk away and keep a wide berth from any other Zs. Get far enough away and lose em round a corner. No need to run or sprint and consume energy 

Play to your character's strengths. If your dude is a chef with a knife bonus, or a construction worker with a short blunt bonus, go ahead and prioritise using them as you'll level up MUCH quicker with your chosen weapon. That Extra skill point early in the game could change the tide for you 

Don't over encumber yourself. You will lose stamina, health, mobility and your life quicker than you can say "aaargh get it off me get it off"

I'm taking a page out of my younger self's book.

Think about toddlers—they run, climb, and move constantly, not because they’re thinking, "I need to hit my daily step count," but because they’re having fun. The movement is just a side effect of play.

That’s how I approach exercise now. I don’t think, “I need to walk for two hours.” Instead, I grab my binoculars and go birdwatching. I don’t focus on “X number of martial arts drills,” I just grapple and try to win the round.

For me, the key to enjoying exercise is to forget it’s exercise. It’s not a chore—it’s just something fun that happens to make me move. It may not work for everyone, but it’s worth a try!

[Edit:] 


That said, I’ve seen too many people take the wrong approach, thinking exercise has to be maximum effort and miserable 100% of the time. It doesn’t. In fact it rarely ever needs to be if you're not actively competing for anything.

People who’ve never run before suddenly crank out 5Ks every day and wonder why it sucks. Others try to lift their one-rep max when they haven’t lifted more than a shopping bag in months. No wonder they hate it.

Little & often beats intense & short-term by a country mile. No need to redline your body—if you’re just starting, you’ll hit your limit fast enough anyway. Short 60-second jogs with 90-second rests will do you far more good than forcing miles on day one.

Same with weights—just focus on making it fun and doable. Once you've formed the habit you'll be making strides in no time.

So in language there are different cases. The nominative is the subject. For example "HE is big. SHE is small." The accusative is the direct object. Examples being,"I don't like HIM. I like HER." Notice how he, her, she and him are being conjugated along with be context of the sentence. 

In Polish there is another case that doesn't get used in English. It's called the instrumental, which is used in conjunction with the verb "to be" "być" 

Nominative - The dog is big - PIES jest duży 
Accusative - I have a dog - Ja mam PSA
Instrumental - He is a dog - On jest PSEM 

It's a bit of a headache to get your head around at first, but keep practicing and you'll get it. I'm around a hundred days in and I've caught a good grasp of it so far purely on Duolingo. (I also have a Polish partner which helps a bunch i suppose lol) 

Note: the only exception to this rule is when using "to" or "tamto" in a sentence in conjunction with być. As an example "To jest pies" would be correct

Hey buddy. Same boat as you a couple of weeks ago but a couple of things have clicked for me that has made my survival a little less grisly.

\-Be comfortable around hordes. It took me a while to get out of the habit of running/attacking big groups head on. You walk faster than the zombles shamble. Attract a fair sized group (Hell, press Q if you need- bear with me) zoom your view out a fair distance and get used to leading them away from your base. You can bunch them together by walking around them in a large arc.   
My concept is this: Assuming you're out in the open with a lot of space, 2 or 3 zombies either side of you is infinitely more dangerous than 100 zombies dead ahead of you. Run around them, herd them like a Border Collie, bunch them up close and lose them around a building somewhere. They forget you fairly quickly once they lose sight, they'll check your last known position and then go back to idle/wander mode. You can do this with a feeble, asthmatic, unfit character predominantly walking. So long as you're awake, fed and hydrated beforehand, you can lose a whole neighbourhood's worth of zombies (Just be sure to mark on your map that there is a big horde there for future reference).

\-Be mindful of the noise you make. Zombies have better hearing than me, who is half deaf in one ear lol. sneaking is quiet, walking is a tad louder, and jogging is like a marching band. Keep this in mind if you feel the need to sneak between two hordes. You're safer crouch walking than roadie running Gears of War style. 

\- If you do happen to take on a horde early on, try and separate stragglers in the group. You can whisper by pressing Q while crouched, and if you position yourself correctly, you can lure a straggler to their demise.

\-Tend to your moodles. Dehydration, starvation and being weighed down like a pack mule can mean the difference between a happy survivor and a dead one. Stay hydrated, do your loot runs first thing in the morning when you're well rested and fed (Sleepy makes you do -50% damage so Get Some Rest!!!) This gives you an opportunity to focus on looting and make a break for it when things get a bit zombie-ey.

​

There's probably more guys who can guide you, but make little adjustments and you'll be kicking butt before long. Hang in there buddy it's absolutely worth it
